prompt: For an angle $\theta$ you know $\sin\theta = 0.6$ and $\cos\theta = 0.8$. What is $\tan\theta$?
explanation: Tangent is height up divided by shadow across: $\tan\theta = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$.
$0.6 \div 0.8 = 0.75$. (Check: $0.6^2 + 0.8^2 = 0.36 + 0.64 = 1$, so these values really can sit on the unit circle.)

alternativeExplanations.title: Turn it into a fraction
steps: 0.6/0.8 is the same as 6/8 after multiplying top and bottom by 10.

alternativeExplanations.title: Read it as slope
steps: tan θ is rise over run for the line from the centre to the point (0.8, 0.6).
It rises 0.6 while it runs 0.8, so the slope is 0.6 ÷ 0.8 = 0.75 — a gentle uphill.
